title: The Drawdown Rule That Saves Traders from Blowing Up
text: When we look at this at that top portfolio level, we generally need to define our account size and whatever our downside budget is, your risk tolerance. Generally speaking, if you want larger returns, you should expect larger potential drawdowns. I say that because everybody would prefer no drawdown, very little drawdown and really big upside. That sets you down a pretty unlikely path. When we define the drawdown, the way I build around that again is via circuit breakers and that's stuff that I monitor myself. And what that means is if we hit that drawdown, I immediately have to start cutting positions because that drawdown for me is defined by a point that shouldn't really happen. If it happens, that means something is happening that I haven't accounted for, which shouldn't really happen. That means something's changed drastically and something's going on that I don't understand and I need to stop it.
